skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - mediate between people and strengthen relationships, adopting the appropriate communication method with stakeholders at all levels - manage stakeholder expectations and moderate difficult discussions about high risk and complex topics, even within constrained timescales - speak on behalf of, and represent the community to, large audiences inside and outside the organisation

You can: - understand and help teams to apply a range of techniques for data profiling - source system analysis from a complex single source - bring multiple data sources together in a conformed model for analysis

You can: - advocate for adoption of unfamiliar and emerging technologies, or familiar technologies in new data contexts, ensuring organisation objectives, user needs, and operational constraints inform decisions - develop organisational capability in data innovation through leadership - anticipate future technology changes and advise how to take advantage of them to realise value from data

You can: - understand different ways to model data to maximise its use and value - ensure data is modelled appropriately, and modelling standards exist and are complied with - understand a number of data integration tools and patterns, and ensure your teams have the support and training needed to use the most appropriate methods - build relationships with other senior data professionals (in fields such as data architecture, data engineering and data science) to share best practice and continually improve data modelling and integration processes and standards

You can: - identify how metadata repositories can support different areas of the organisation - communicate the value of metadata repositories - set up robust governance processes to keep repositories up to date

You can: - anticipate problems and defend against them at the right time - understand how a problem fits into the larger picture - identify and describe problems, and help others to describe them - build problem-solving capabilities in others

skill: Programming and build (data and analytics engineering)
expected_level_description: You can: - set standards for programming tools and techniques - select appropriate development methods for a problem - advise on the application of standards and methods that ensure security, maintainability and compliance - take technical responsibility for all stages of a software development project, providing technical advice and guidance to stakeholders
You can: - review requirements and specifications, and define test conditions - identify issues and risks associated with work - analyse and report test activities and results

skill: Turning business problems into data design
expected_level_description: You can: - design data architecture that deals with problems across the enterprise - work across all organisational subject areas and internal and external programmes

You can: - shape organisational strategy using a deep understanding of the health and care system - represent the organisation with health and care partners and leaders - anticipate how policy and service changes will affect digital services and care

You can: - lead data protection impact assessments and information sharing agreements - advise teams on lawful basis, consent, confidentiality, and retention - investigate incidents and recommend improvements
You can: - set data quality standards for the organisation and its partners - lead data quality improvement programmes

You can: - design data models and reference sets using clinical terminologies - map between terminologies and classifications, and explain the limits of a mapping - advise teams on terminology use in products and analytics
You can: - lead managers and shape the culture of a large area - design workforce plans and organisational change - coach leaders and resolve complex people issues
You can: - hold and manage a budget, forecasting and explaining variances - build a business case with costs and benefits
